| REQ-ECO-6187 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Event Namespace: Axiom runtime events use: runtime.* Compiler-generated events use: compiler.* Application events use application-defined namespaces. | 0827 §602.137 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6188 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Event Collision: Event IDs must be scoped by diagnostic namespace or generated through a linker-level allocation mechanism. | 0827 §602.138 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6189 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User-Defined Diagnostic Types: Axiom permits: struct DiagnosticValue { ... } only when it implements a restricted diagnostic encoding trait. The encoder must have explicit bounded behavior. | 0827 §602.139 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6190 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Arbitrary Display Execution: Logging an object must not invoke an arbitrary unbounded method. The diagnostic encoder contract must define: maximum size maximum recursion maximum execution behavior | 0827 §602.140 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6191 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Recursive Data: Diagnostic serialization detects cycles. Example: A → B → A must not recurse forever. | 0827 §602.141 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6192 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Maximum Diagnostic Depth: Default: max_depth = 8 Configuration may change this within bounded limits. | 0827 §602.142 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6193 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Maximum Event Size: Every event has a maximum encoded size. Example: 64 KiB Events exceeding the limit are truncated or rejected according to policy. | 0827 §602.143 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6194 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Truncation Metadata: Truncated events indicate: truncated = true original_size = N when known. | 0827 §602.144 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6195 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Binary Data: Binary payloads must be bounded. Large buffers should not be logged directly. Instead: log.info("packet", { size: packet.len, hash: hash(packet) }) | 0827 §602.145 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6196 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Hashing: A diagnostic helper may compute: diagnostic_hash(data) to identify repeated payloads without storing the payload. | 0827 §602.146 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6197 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Rate Limiting: High-frequency events may be rate-limited. Example: logger.rate_limit( event = "network.retry", max_events = 100, interval = 1s ) | 0827 §602.147 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6198 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Suppression Summary: Suppressed events should produce a summary: network.retry suppressed=2381 so filtering does not hide the fact that an abnormal volume occurred. | 0827 §602.148 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6199 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Burst Protection: A logger must protect the application from event storms. The diagnostic subsystem itself must not become an outage amplifier. | 0827 §602.149 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6200 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Per-Category Budgets: Applications may define: network: 1 MB/min database: 512 KB/min graphics: 2 MB/min | 0827 §602.150 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6201 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Global Diagnostic Budget: A global budget may cap: bytes events CPU time memory allocated to diagnostics. | 0827 §602.151 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6202 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic CPU Budget: The runtime should expose configuration for limiting expensive formatting/tracing. | 0827 §602.152 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6203 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — High-Frequency Path: For hot loops: if diagnostic.enabled(.trace) { ... } must allow the compiler to hoist or eliminate the check when possible. | 0827 §602.153 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6204 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compile-Time Category Elimination: If a category is disabled at compile time: log.trace("physics", ...) can become zero instructions. | 0827 §602.154 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6205 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Constant Propagation: Diagnostic configuration should be represented in compiler-visible constants where practical. | 0827 §602.155 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6206 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Link-Time Elimination: Unused diagnostic sinks should be removed by linker dead-code elimination. | 0827 §602.156 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6207 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Hidden Global Initialization Requirement: Axiom diagnostics should use explicit runtime initialization. The runtime may initialize mandatory crash facilities before application entry. | 0827 §602.157 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6208 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Initialization Order: Startup: native process ↓ minimal runtime ↓ crash handler ↓ emergency buffer ↓ diagnostic core ↓ configuration ↓ application | 0827 §602.158 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6209 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Shutdown Order: Shutdown: application ↓ flush logs ↓ flush traces ↓ close exporters ↓ close diagnostic store The crash handler remains available until the process is actually terminating. | 0827 §602.159 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6210 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Abrupt Exit: For: process.exit_now() normal flushing is not guaranteed. The API must document this explicitly. | 0827 §602.160 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6211 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Graceful Exit: For normal shutdown: process.exit() the runtime attempts configured flush operations. | 0827 §602.161 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6212 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Clock: Events contain: wall-clock timestamp monotonic timestamp Wall-clock time is for humans. Monotonic time is for duration ordering. | 0827 §602.162 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6213 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Clock Failure: If wall-clock time is unavailable: timestamp = unknown but monotonic diagnostic ordering remains available. | 0827 §602.163 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6214 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Time Synchronization: The diagnostic subsystem does not assume the wall clock is synchronized. Distributed systems must use trace IDs and monotonic local durations where appropriate. | 0827 §602.164 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6215 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Thread Identity: Thread IDs are captured as native identifiers. The runtime may additionally expose logical task IDs. | 0827 §602.165 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6216 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Task Identity: For async execution: TaskId may be associated with diagnostics. This is especially useful when many tasks share one OS thread. | 0827 §602.166 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6217 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Scheduler Integration: The scheduler may expose: task creation task suspension task resume task completion task failure as trace events. These events are optional. | 0827 §602.167 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6218 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Deadlock Diagnostics: The runtime may provide a diagnostic snapshot of known synchronization state. It must not attempt unsafe lock acquisition from a crash handler. | 0827 §602.168 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6219 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hang Detection: Optional watchdog: application heartbeat ↓ watchdog ↓ no progress ↓ diagnostic snapshot This is not a mandatory crash mechanism. | 0827 §602.169 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6220 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Watchdog Safety: The watchdog must be bounded and must not terminate healthy applications merely because they are intentionally idle. | 0827 §602.170 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6221 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Health API: Applications may expose: trait HealthProvider { fn health() -> HealthStatus } | 0827 §602.171 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6222 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Health Status: enum HealthStatus { healthy degraded unavailable unknown } | 0827 §602.172 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6223 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Health vs Application Health: These are distinct. Diagnostic subsystem health answers: Can diagnostics function? Application health answers: Is the application functioning? | 0827 §602.173 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6224 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Self-Test: Optional: diagnostics.self_test() checks: - ring buffer; - sinks; - storage; - symbol metadata; - crash artifact directory. | 0827 §602.174 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6225 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Self-Test Safety: Self-test must not intentionally trigger an actual process crash. | 0827 §602.175 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6226 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Test Crash Capture: Development builds may expose a controlled test: diagnostics.test_crash() It must be explicitly enabled and unavailable in normal production builds unless intentionally configured. | 0827 §602.176 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6227 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Artifact Naming: Recommended: <AppId>_<BuildId>_<Timestamp>_<CrashId>.axcrash | 0827 §602.177 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6228 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash ID: Each crash receives a locally unique identifier. It must not require network connectivity. | 0827 §602.178 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6229 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — UUID Dependency: The implementation may use UUID-like identifiers but the runtime must not require an external UUID library. | 0827 §602.179 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6230 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Artifact Storage: Default location comes from BOOTSTRAP-601 deployment configuration. The runtime must support platform-appropriate application data directories. | 0827 §602.180 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6231 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Storage Security: Crash artifacts should use restrictive permissions where supported. | 0827 §602.181 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6232 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Storage Quota: Diagnostic storage has a configurable quota. Example: max_total = 128 MB | 0827 §602.182 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6233 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Retention: Retention policy may be: count-based size-based age-based | 0827 §602.183 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6234 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Artifact Corruption Recovery: At startup, incomplete artifacts are: detected validated marked incomplete retained or deleted according to retention policy. | 0827 §602.184 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6235 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Partial Crash Artifact: A partial artifact is still useful. The format therefore supports: complete = false and independently parseable sections. | 0827 §602.185 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6236 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Emergency Artifact Writer: The crash writer should use: preallocated buffers direct/native file APIs fixed-size metadata bounded loops where platform-safe. | 0827 §602.186 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6237 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Writer Failure: If file writing fails: attempt alternate location then: attempt platform-native crash mechanism then terminate. | 0827 §602.187 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6238 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Infinite Recovery: Crash reporting must never repeatedly attempt recovery after fatal corruption. | 0827 §602.188 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6239 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Handler Isolation: The application must not be able to accidentally disable mandatory crash capture through ordinary logger configuration. | 0827 §602.189 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6240 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Permissions: Applications may disable optional diagnostics. They must not be able to violate OS/platform security restrictions. | 0827 §602.190 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6241 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User Data Policy: The runtime does not automatically inspect arbitrary application memory for crash reporting. Only explicitly defined regions are captured. | 0827 §602.191 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6242 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Snapshot: Full process-memory dumps are optional and platform-controlled. They are not part of the minimal `.axcrash` requirement. | 0827 §602.192 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6243 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Large Memory Applications: Applications with huge memory footprints must not incur proportional diagnostic overhead during normal operation. | 0827 §602.193 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6244 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Capture Complexity: Target: O(number of captured frames + number of bounded metadata records) No operation should scan the entire heap by default. | 0827 §602.194 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6245 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Normal Logging Complexity: For accepted fixed-size primitive events: O(event_size) For disabled events: O(1) | 0827 §602.195 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6246 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Requirements: Minimal runtime diagnostics should have bounded memory: emergency crash buffer + configured ring buffers + optional queues No unbounded diagnostic memory structure is permitted. | 0827 §602.196 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6247 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — ABI Stability: Public diagnostic structures intended for native library interoperability must have explicit ABI versions. | 0827 §602.197 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6248 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — C ABI Interoperability: Axiom may expose a minimal C-compatible diagnostic ABI for interoperability. This must not require a C runtime for Axiom applications. | 0827 §602.198 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6249 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native Callback ABI: Callbacks crossing diagnostic boundaries must declare: calling convention threading contract lifetime error behavior | 0827 §602.199 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6250 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Handling: Diagnostic APIs should return explicit errors where an operation can fail. Example: let result = diagnostics.snapshot("support") Possible errors: storage_unavailable quota_exceeded serialization_failed permission_denied busy | 0827 §602.200 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6251 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic API Must Not Panic: Ordinary diagnostic failures should not themselves trigger application panic. Example: logger.flush() must not recursively crash the application merely because disk I/O failed. | 0827 §602.201 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6252 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Recursive Failure Protection: The diagnostic subsystem has a final emergency path: normal diagnostic ↓ failure minimal diagnostic ↓ failure raw termination | 0827 §602.202 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6253 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Acceptance Criteria: BOOTSTRAP-602 is complete when the Axiom implementation can demonstrate: ### Logging - structured logs; - severity levels; - category filtering; - event IDs; - lazy arguments; - compile-time elimination; - bounded events; - thread-safe logging. ### Tracing - trace IDs; - spans; - bounded trace buffers; - sampling; - async-task correlation. ### Crash handling - native fault capture; - panic capture; - assertion capture; - register capture; - bounded stack capture; - module identity; - build identity; - crash artifact generation. ### Security - secret values cannot be logged accidentally; - configuration secrets remain protected; - environment capture is allowlisted; - command-line secrets are not dumped by default. ### Resilience - logger failure does not normally crash the application; - disk-full behavior is bounded; - crash handler does not depend on ordinary heap allocation; - recursive crash handling terminates safely; - partial artifacts remain parseable. ### Toolchain - compiler emits diagnostic metadata; - linker preserves diagnostic identities; - symbols can be matched to crash artifacts; - unused diagnostic components can be dead-stripped. ### Platform At minimum, the architecture must support: Windows Linux macOS iOS Android WASM through platform adapters. | 0827 §602.203 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6254 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required Compiler/Runtime Components: Implementation should produce: axiom.diagnostics.core axiom.diagnostics.logging axiom.diagnostics.trace axiom.diagnostics.crash axiom.diagnostics.symbols axiom.diagnostics.storage axiom.diagnostics.export These are logical components, not necessarily separate binaries. | 0827 §602.204 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6255 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required Tooling: The Axiom toolchain should provide: ax log ax crash ax symbolize ax diagnose ax dump Possible operations: ax crash inspect file.axcrash ax symbolize file.axcrash ax diagnose build/ | 0827 §602.205 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6256 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax crash inspect`: Displays: application build platform fault thread stack modules recent logs trace checkpoint configuration fingerprint | 0827 §602.206 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6257 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax symbolize`: Consumes: .axcrash .axsym and produces source-level stack information. | 0827 §602.207 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6258 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax crash export`: Converts: .axcrash to: JSON text diagnostic package without changing the original artifact. | 0827 §602.208 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6259 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax diagnose`: Can analyze: - crash artifacts; - logs; - trace data; - build metadata; - symbol files. It should remain a toolchain feature rather than part of the application runtime. | 0827 §602.209 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6260 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AI-Friendly Diagnostics: Axiom diagnostic artifacts should be machine-readable. The canonical structured representation must expose: stable IDs schema versions explicit types source locations build identity causal relationships This allows AI tooling to reason over failures without relying exclusively on human-formatted logs. | 0827 §602.210 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6261 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Causality: Events may reference: parent event trace span request task checkpoint This enables reconstruction such as: request ↓ task ↓ database query ↓ timeout ↓ retry ↓ panic ↓ crash | 0827 §602.211 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6262 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Failure Chain: The diagnostic runtime may assign: FailureId to related failures. Example: FailureId = F-1827 All related events can reference the same failure. | 0827 §602.212 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6263 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Context: Axiom errors may optionally carry: struct ErrorContext { error_code source cause trace_id span_id } | 0827 §602.213 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6264 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Cause Chain: Errors may form: application error ↓ database error ↓ network error ↓ OS error The chain must be bounded. | 0827 §602.214 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6265 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cause Depth: Default maximum: 16 to prevent pathological recursive error chains. | 0827 §602.215 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6266 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Serialization: Error chains can be serialized into crash artifacts and snapshots. Secrets remain filtered. | 0827 §602.216 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6267 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Version Compatibility: Diagnostic readers should support multiple artifact versions where practical. The artifact format must explicitly identify its version. | 0827 §602.217 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6268 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Schema Migration: Axiom tooling may migrate: .axcrash v1 to a newer logical representation without modifying the original artifact. | 0827 §602.218 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6269 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Long-Term Preservation: Crash artifacts must be interpretable even if the original application is no longer installed. Therefore the artifact must contain enough metadata to identify: format platform architecture build runtime module identities | 0827 §602.219 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6270 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory Cloud: Axiom's diagnostics architecture is fully functional without: cloud vendor account telemetry server internet | 0827 §602.220 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6271 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory Third-Party Runtime: The final native executable must not require an external logging or crash-reporting runtime merely to execute. | 0827 §602.221 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6272 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Determinism: Diagnostic behavior must be deterministic with respect to: - filtering; - event schema; - artifact encoding; - retention policy. Timestamps and runtime scheduling are naturally nondeterministic. | 0827 §602.222 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6273 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Performance Target: The target for disabled logging: effectively zero runtime overhead when compile-time elimination is possible. For enabled primitive logging: bounded O(event_size) with no mandatory heap allocation. | 0827 §602.223 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6274 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Performance: Crash capture must prioritize: safety > completeness > convenience The runtime must prefer a partial valid crash artifact over risking recursive failure while attempting a perfect one. | 0827 §602.224 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6275 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Relationship to BOOTSTRAP-600: BOOTSTRAP-600 owns: application state session checkpoint recovery crash-resilient state BOOTSTRAP-602 only records diagnostic references to that state. It must not become the state-management subsystem. | 0827 §602.225 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6276 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Relationship to BOOTSTRAP-601: BOOTSTRAP-601 owns: configuration profiles environment secrets deployment identity BOOTSTRAP-602 consumes safe identifiers from it. It must not duplicate configuration resolution. | 0827 §602.226 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6277 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Boundary Rule: The three subsystems therefore remain: 600 = What state does the application have? 601 = How is the application configured/deployed? 602 = What happened while the application was running? This separation is mandatory. | 0827 §602.227 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6278 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Architectural Result: After BOOTSTRAP-602, a native Axiom application has a complete foundational observability path: APPLICATION │ ┌─────────┼─────────┐ ▼         ▼         ▼ STATE      CONFIG   DIAGNOSTICS 600        601        602 │          │          │ └──────────┼──────────┘ ▼ BUILD IDENTITY │ ▼ FAILURE EVIDENCE │ ┌──────────┼───────────┐ ▼          ▼           ▼ LOGS       TRACE       CRASH │          │           │ └──────────┼───────────┘ ▼ .AXCRASH / STORE This creates the minimum native foundation required for an Axiom application to be diagnosable in production without depending on third-party infrastructure. | 0827 §602.228 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6279 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Task Completion: **BOOTSTRAP-602 is complete.** The specification now establishes: - native structured logging; - compile-time log elimination; - runtime filtering; - structured diagnostic events; - trace/span infrastructure; - crash-safe emergency buffers; - native fault capture; - panic/assertion diagnostics; - stack/register/module capture; - symbol identity; - `.axcrash` artifact architecture; - privacy and secret protection; - configuration/state correlation; - bounded logging and tracing; - diagnostic snapshots; - health/watchdog foundations; - platform adapters; - compiler/linker integration; - AI-readable diagnostic metadata; - offline-first operation; - no mandatory third-party runtime dependency. **Next task: `BOOTSTRAP-603 — NATIVE APPLICATION SECURITY, IDENTITY, CAPABILITY & TRUST RUNTIME 5.0`** .: BOOTSTRAP-602 đã nối đúng sau 601. Chuỗi tiếp theo là **BOOTSTRAP-603**, không cần thay đổi số thứ tự hay quay lại các task trước. | 0827 §602.229 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6280 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Purpose: BOOTSTRAP-603 defines the foundational security model of Axiom applications. The subsystem governs: 1. application identity; 2. execution identity; 3. capabilities; 4. resource permissions; 5. trust boundaries; 6. privilege boundaries; 7. secure handles; 8. cryptographic primitives; 9. secure randomness; 10. credential isolation; 11. process and module trust; 12. sandbox integration; 13. permission requests; 14. authorization decisions; 15. security auditing; 16. secure IPC boundaries; 17. platform security adapters; 18. secure failure behavior. The design must avoid turning Axiom into a complicated security framework. The fundamental rule is: > **Code should possess authority explicitly rather than receiving unlimited authority implicitly.** | 0828 §603.0 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6281 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Principles: Axiom security follows: least privilege explicit authority deny by default capability-oriented access immutable identity bounded resources secure failure auditable decisions platform integration no mandatory cloud | 0828 §603.1 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6282 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Implicit Universal Authority: An ordinary Axiom application must not automatically receive unrestricted access to: - filesystem; - network; - processes; - devices; - credentials; - environment; - system configuration. Access must come from the platform or an explicitly declared capability. | 0828 §603.2 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6283 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Model: The primary abstraction is: Capability<T> A capability represents authority to perform a specific class of operation. Example: Capability<FileSystem> Capability<Network> Capability<Camera> Capability<Process> Possessing the capability is the authorization. | 0828 §603.3 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6284 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Is Not a String: This is forbidden as the primary authorization mechanism: if permissions.contains("filesystem.write") { ... } Instead: fn save(file: FileWriteCapability, data: Bytes) The type system carries authority. | 0828 §603.4 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6285 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Non-Forgery: Application code must not be able to construct an arbitrary privileged capability. For example: Capability<FileSystem>() is invalid unless the compiler/runtime provides a legitimate authority source. | 0828 §603.5 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6286 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Origin: A capability originates from: platform application manifest parent capability user authorization secure subsystem trusted bootstrap | 0828 §603.6 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6287 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Attenuation: A capability may be restricted. Example: let full = filesystem let images = full.subtree("/images") The resulting capability has no authority outside `/images`. | 0828 §603.7 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6288 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Monotonicity: Deriving a child capability must never increase authority. child.authority ⊆ parent.authority This is a core invariant. | 0828 §603.8 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6289 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Revocation: Capabilities may be revocable. capability.revoke() A revoked capability must fail future operations. Already completed operations are not retroactively undone. | 0828 §603.9 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6290 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Lifetime: Capabilities are ordinary native values with explicit lifetime. They do not require garbage collection. | 0828 §603.10 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6291 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Transfer: A capability can be transferred between trusted execution contexts if the API explicitly allows it. Example: worker.send(capability) The sender may optionally relinquish its authority. | 0828 §603.11 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6292 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Duplication: Duplication policy depends on capability type. Some capabilities may be: copyable shareable move-only non-transferable | 0828 §603.12 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6293 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Move-Only Security Capabilities: Highly privileged capabilities should support move semantics: let cap2 = move cap1 After transfer: cap1 = invalid cap2 = valid | 0828 §603.13 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6294 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Scope: Capabilities may be scoped to: application process thread task session resource operation | 0828 §603.14 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6295 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Resource Capability: A resource capability may represent: file directory socket device process memory region IPC endpoint credential cryptographic key | 0828 §603.15 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6296 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — File Capability: Example: FileReadCapability FileWriteCapability DirectoryCapability Read and write authority are separate. | 0828 §603.16 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6297 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Path Authority: A file capability should preferably contain a canonicalized authority boundary rather than repeatedly trusting arbitrary path strings. | 0828 §603.17 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6298 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Path Traversal Protection: A capability restricted to: /app/data must not permit: /app/data/../secrets to escape its authority. Canonicalization occurs before authorization. | 0828 §603.18 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6299 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Symlink / Reparse Boundaries: Platform-specific path mechanisms such as: - symbolic links; - junctions; - reparse points; must not silently bypass a capability boundary. The runtime adapter must define secure resolution semantics. | 0828 §603.19 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6300 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — File Operation API: Preferred: file = fs.open(capability, relative_path) rather than: file = open("/arbitrary/path") for sandboxed applications. | 0828 §603.20 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6301 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Network Capability: Network authority is explicit. Possible forms: NetworkConnectCapability NetworkListenCapability NetworkDnsCapability | 0828 §603.21 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6302 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Network Attenuation: A network capability may be restricted by: protocol host port address family direction Example: let api = network.connect_to("api.example.com", 443) | 0828 §603.22 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6303 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — DNS Authority: DNS access may be separated from raw socket authority. This permits tighter sandboxing. | 0828 §603.23 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6304 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Process Capability: Process authority includes: spawn inspect signal terminate debug These are separate capabilities. | 0828 §603.24 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6305 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Process Spawning: Axiom should not expose unrestricted shell execution as the normal process API. Preferred: process.spawn( executable, arguments, capability ) | 0828 §603.25 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6306 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Shell Independence: The runtime must not require: cmd.exe powershell /bin/sh /bin/bash to launch ordinary processes. | 0828 §603.26 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6307 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Argument Safety: Process arguments are passed as structured argument arrays. The runtime must not concatenate them into a shell command string. | 0828 §603.27 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6308 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Environment Inheritance: Environment inheritance must be explicit. Example: process.spawn( env = environment.minimal() ) | 0828 §603.28 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6309 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Credential Capability: Credentials are represented as opaque values. Example: Credential<T> They must not automatically convert to: String Bytes DiagnosticValue | 0828 §603.29 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6310 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Integration: BOOTSTRAP-601 `Secret<T>` remains the configuration/secret representation. BOOTSTRAP-603 defines runtime authority for using the secret. | 0828 §603.30 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6311 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Access: A secret should be accessed through a restricted operation: secret.with_value(/value/ { use(value) }) This allows future implementations to minimize exposure. | 0828 §603.31 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6312 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Memory: Sensitive memory may require: non-swappable memory zeroization restricted copying when supported by the platform and appropriate for the secret class. | 0828 §603.32 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6313 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Zeroization: API: secure.zeroize(buffer) The compiler must prevent optimization from removing a required security wipe. | 0828 §603.33 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6314 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Copying: The runtime should discourage unnecessary copies of secret data. The type system may mark sensitive values as: move-only non-copyable | 0828 §603.34 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6315 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic Boundary: Axiom provides cryptographic primitives as native runtime facilities. However, application-level protocols must not be silently invented by the runtime. | 0828 §603.35 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6316 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic API Categories: Core categories: hash MAC KDF AEAD signature key generation randomness constant-time comparison | 0828 §603.36 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6317 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hash API: Example: hash.sha256(data) The API returns a fixed-size digest type. | 0828 §603.37 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6318 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Typed Digest: Example: Digest<sha256> rather than a generic untyped byte array. | 0828 §603.38 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6319 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — MAC: Example: mac.hmac_sha256(key, data) Keys remain opaque. | 0828 §603.39 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6320 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — KDF: Supported conceptual interface: kdf.derive( key, salt, context, output_length ) | 0828 §603.40 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6321 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AEAD: Authenticated encryption provides: aead.encrypt(key, nonce, plaintext, associated_data) aead.decrypt(key, nonce, ciphertext, associated_data) Decryption failure must not expose partially authenticated plaintext. | 0828 §603.41 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6322 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Nonce Handling: Nonce rules must be explicit. The runtime must provide safe nonce generation where the algorithm requires uniqueness/randomness. | 0828 §603.42 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6323 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Signature API: Example: signature.sign(private_key, data) signature.verify(public_key, data, signature) | 0828 §603.43 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6324 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Key Types: Keys must be strongly typed: PrivateKey<Algorithm> PublicKey<Algorithm> SymmetricKey<Algorithm> | 0828 §603.44 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6325 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Algorithm Agility: The API must identify algorithms explicitly. Avoid: encrypt(data) where the algorithm is hidden. Prefer: aead.encrypt(.AES256_GCM, ...) or an equivalent typed key API. | 0828 §603.45 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6326 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic Primitive Policy: The runtime must distinguish: available algorithm approved algorithm legacy algorithm insecure algorithm Applications should receive explicit diagnostics when using deprecated primitives. | 0828 §603.46 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6327 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Randomness: API: random.secure(bytes) must use the platform's cryptographically secure random source. | 0828 §603.47 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6328 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — General Randomness: A separate API: random.fast() may exist for simulation and non-security workloads. It must not be advertised as cryptographically secure. | 0828 §603.48 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6329 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Random Type Separation: Security-sensitive APIs should reject ordinary pseudo-random generators where secure randomness is required. | 0828 §603.49 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6330 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Constant-Time Comparison: API: secure.equals(a, b) provides comparison suitable for sensitive byte sequences. | 0828 §603.50 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6331 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Timing Resistance: The runtime should avoid obvious early-exit behavior for cryptographic comparisons. The exact guarantees are platform/compiler dependent and must be documented. | 0828 §603.51 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6332 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Key Lifecycle: Keys have explicit states: generated active suspended revoked destroyed | 0828 §603.52 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6333 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Key Destruction: Destroying a key must invalidate its capability and, where possible, clear sensitive memory. | 0828 §603.53 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6334 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hardware-Backed Keys: The architecture supports opaque references to platform key stores. Examples: TPM Secure Enclave Android Keystore platform credential store The core runtime must not assume any particular hardware exists. | 0828 §603.54 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6335 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hardware Key Abstraction: HardwareKey<Algorithm> can expose permitted cryptographic operations without exposing raw key material. | 0828 §603.55 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6336 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Identity: An application has: AppIdentity containing: application_id publisher_id build_id platform_identity | 0828 §603.56 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6337 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Application ID: The application ID is stable across builds of the same logical application. | 0828 §603.57 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6338 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Build ID: The build ID identifies a particular executable build. This integrates with BOOTSTRAP-602 diagnostics. | 0828 §603.58 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6339 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Publisher Identity: A publisher identity identifies the signing authority or development authority associated with an application. | 0828 §603.59 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6340 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Signing Identity: A signed build may contain: publisher certificate/key identity signature metadata build identity The runtime can expose this information without requiring a network lookup. | 0828 §603.60 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6341 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Code Signing: Axiom toolchains should support platform-native code-signing formats. The compiler itself does not need to implement every external signing service. | 0828 §603.61 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6342 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Signature Verification: API: trust.verify_signature(binary, public_key) returns a structured result. | 0828 §603.62 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6343 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Result: enum TrustStatus { trusted untrusted invalid unknown } These are descriptive security states, not political or subjective judgments. | 0828 §603.63 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6344 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Chain: A verification result may include: root intermediate leaf artifact and failure reason. | 0828 §603.64 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6345 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Automatic Trust of Local Files: A local executable is not automatically trusted merely because it exists on disk. | 0828 §603.65 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6346 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Module Identity: Each native module may expose: ModuleId BuildId PublisherId SignatureStatus | 0828 §603.66 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6347 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic Library Loading: Dynamic loading requires an explicit capability in restricted environments. | 0828 §603.67 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6348 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Library Trust Policy: An application may require: loader.require_publisher(PublisherId) or: loader.require_signature(...) before loading a module. | 0828 §603.68 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6349 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dependency Verification: A deployment manifest may specify expected: module ID version hash publisher | 0828 §603.69 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6350 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dependency Mismatch: A mismatch should produce a structured security error. The runtime must not silently substitute an unrelated module. | 0828 §603.70 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6351 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hash Verification: Example: module.require_hash(expected) This protects against unexpected binary replacement. | 0828 §603.71 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6352 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — TOCTOU Protection: Security-sensitive resource access must minimize: check ↓ resource changes ↓ use windows. Where platform APIs support atomic secure operations, the runtime should use them. | 0828 §603.72 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6353 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Handle: Axiom uses opaque handles for privileged native resources: Handle<T> The numeric native handle is not directly exposed by default. | 0828 §603.73 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6354 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Handle Ownership: Handles have explicit ownership: owned borrowed shared invalid This should integrate with Axiom's broader resource/lifetime model without introducing a mandatory borrow checker. | 0828 §603.74 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6355 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Handle Closing: Example: with fs.open(cap, "data.bin") as file { ... } leaves scope and closes the handle deterministically. | 0828 §603.75 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6356 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No GC Requirement: Security-sensitive resource cleanup must not depend on garbage collection. | 0828 §603.76 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6357 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Double Close: Closing an owned resource twice is invalid. Debug builds should detect it. Release behavior should be deterministic and safe. | 0828 §603.77 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6358 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Tokens: Internally, capabilities may be represented using: opaque pointer native handle index kernel token sealed structure The representation is platform-specific. | 0828 §603.78 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6359 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Forgery Resistance: The representation must make accidental or ordinary application-level forgery impractical. | 0828 §603.79 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6360 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Safety Boundary: The security runtime does not replace Axiom's memory model. Instead it defines privileged-resource boundaries independent of whether the application uses: - stack values; - owned values; - flat memory; - native handles; - shared memory. | 0828 §603.80 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6361 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unsafe Code: Axiom may provide: unsafe { ... } for low-level operations. Unsafe code does not automatically gain all capabilities. | 0828 §603.81 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6362 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unsafe ≠ Privileged: This distinction is mandatory: unsafe ≠ authorized Unsafe code can violate memory/type invariants within its authority, but cannot manufacture platform permissions. | 0828 §603.82 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6363 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Boundaries and FFI: An FFI call inherits only the capabilities explicitly passed to it. Calling native code does not grant universal Axiom authority. | 0828 §603.83 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6364 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native ABI Boundary: FFI interfaces should declare security requirements. Example: extern fn camera_capture( camera: CameraCapability ) | 0828 §603.84 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6365 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — IPC Capability: IPC endpoints are represented as: IpcCapability<T> | 0828 §603.85 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6366 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — IPC Authentication: An IPC endpoint may authenticate the peer using: process identity application identity publisher identity session identity cryptographic identity platform identity | 0828 §603.86 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6367 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — IPC Authorization: Authentication answers: Who are you? Authorization answers: What are you allowed to do? Axiom must keep these concepts separate. | 0828 §603.87 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6368 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Peer Identity: struct PeerIdentity { app_id publisher_id process_id session_id } Fields vary by platform. | 0828 §603.88 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6369 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure IPC Handshake: A secure channel may establish: peer identity channel identity capabilities session key | 0828 §603.89 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6370 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Passing over IPC: A trusted process may explicitly transfer authority through IPC. The receiver receives only the transferred capability. | 0828 §603.90 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6371 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Revocation over IPC: Revocation must propagate to transferred capabilities where the platform supports centralized capability tracking. | 0828 §603.91 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6372 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Sandboxing: Axiom applications may declare a sandbox profile. Example: filesystem.read network.connect camera microphone gpu process.spawn | 0828 §603.92 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6373 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Manifest Integration: BOOTSTRAP-601 deployment manifests may declare required capabilities. Example: capabilities: filesystem: read: app_data network: connect: api.example.com:443 | 0828 §603.93 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6374 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Manifest vs Runtime: Manifest declaration expresses: what the application requests Runtime capability expresses: what the application actually possesses They are distinct. | 0828 §603.94 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6375 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Denial: If a requested capability is denied: CapabilityError.denied is returned. | 0828 §603.95 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6376 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Silent Escalation: The runtime must never automatically retry a denied capability using a more privileged mechanism. | 0828 §603.96 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6377 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User Permission: Interactive permissions may involve the user or operating system. The runtime exposes the result: permission.request(camera) without deciding whether the user should grant it. | 0828 §603.97 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6378 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission State: enum PermissionState { granted denied restricted unavailable unknown } | 0828 §603.98 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6379 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission Revocation: Applications must handle permissions disappearing after they were previously granted. | 0828 §603.99 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6380 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission Cache: The runtime may cache permission state briefly but must not assume permanent authorization. | 0828 §603.100 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6381 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Defaults: Default policy: no capability unless explicitly granted by platform/runtime. | 0828 §603.101 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6382 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Development Mode: Development builds may request broader capabilities, but development mode must not silently weaken production security. | 0828 §603.102 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6383 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Debugger Capability: Debugging another process is a privileged capability. It must be separate from ordinary process inspection. | 0828 §603.103 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6384 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Inspection: Reading another process's memory requires explicit authorization. The runtime must not provide unrestricted memory inspection as a normal API. | 0828 §603.104 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6385 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Code Injection: Dynamic code injection is not a normal Axiom capability. If a platform/debugging environment supports it, it belongs to explicitly privileged tooling. | 0828 §603.105 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6386 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic Code Loading: Runtime-generated executable code must be controlled by the execution/security layer. A normal application cannot silently convert arbitrary writable memory into executable code. | 0828 §603.106 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6387 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — W^X: Where the platform supports it, executable memory should follow: write OR execute rather than: write AND execute simultaneously. | 0828 §603.107 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6388 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — JIT Capability: JIT execution is a separate capability: Capability<JitExecution> This is especially relevant for: - scripting; - dynamic compilation; - GPU kernels; - runtime code generation. | 0828 §603.108 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6389 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Executable Memory: The runtime should expose controlled allocation: exec_memory.allocate(capability, size) with explicit permission transitions. | 0828 §603.109 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6390 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Protection: Memory regions may transition: read/write read-only read/execute according to platform constraints. | 0828 §603.110 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6391 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Guard Pages: Security-sensitive native allocations may use guard pages where practical. | 0828 §603.111 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6392 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Stack Protection: The toolchain should support platform stack-protection mechanisms where appropriate. | 0828 §603.112 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6393 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Integer Overflow Policy: The security runtime does not redefine Axiom arithmetic semantics. However, security-sensitive code should have explicit checked arithmetic APIs. Example: checked.add(a, b) | 0828 §603.113 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6394 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Bounds Validation: Native APIs must validate: length offset count alignment handle state before unsafe operations. | 0828 §603.114 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6395 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Integer-to-Size Conversion: Conversions into native allocation/index sizes must provide checked forms. | 0828 §603.115 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6396 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Serialization Security: Binary deserialization must enforce: maximum size maximum depth maximum collection count maximum string size | 0828 §603.116 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6397 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Arbitrary Deserialization Code: Deserializing external data must not execute arbitrary constructors or methods. | 0828 §603.117 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6398 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Parser Isolation: Security-sensitive parsers should operate with bounded resource budgets. | 0828 §603.118 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6399 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Resource Exhaustion: Capabilities may include quotas: max file size max network bytes max processes max memory max CPU max IPC messages | 0828 §603.119 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6400 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Quota Model: CapabilityQuota { bytes operations duration concurrency } | 0828 §603.120 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6401 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Quota Enforcement: A quota violation returns: SecurityError.quota_exceeded rather than silently truncating a security-sensitive operation. | 0828 §603.121 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6402 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Rate-Limited Capabilities: Capabilities may enforce operation rates. Example: 100 requests/minute | 0828 §603.122 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6403 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Events: Security-sensitive decisions should integrate with BOOTSTRAP-602: security.capability.granted security.capability.denied security.permission.changed security.signature.invalid security.module.rejected security.credential.access | 0828 §603.123 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6404 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Privacy: Audit events must not expose: - passwords; - private keys; - raw access tokens; - secret configuration values. | 0828 §603.124 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6405 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Integrity: High-security deployments may require tamper-evident audit records. This can use chained hashes: H(event_n // H(event_n-1)) | 0828 §603.125 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6406 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Storage: Audit logs remain separate from ordinary application logs. This prevents normal log rotation from accidentally destroying security records. | 0828 §603.126 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6407 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Event Severity: Security events use ordinary BOOTSTRAP-602 severity levels but may additionally carry a security classification. | 0828 §603.127 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6408 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Classification: Example: enum SecurityEventClass { authentication authorization capability integrity credential sandbox cryptography } | 0828 §603.128 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6409 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Authentication API: The core runtime provides primitives for authenticating identities but does not mandate a universal account system. | 0828 §603.129 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6410 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Identity Provider: An application may integrate: IdentityProvider which returns an opaque identity. | 0828 §603.130 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6411 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Identity Object: Identity { id issuer attributes } Attributes must be explicitly typed and bounded. | 0828 §603.131 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6412 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Authentication Result: enum AuthenticationResult { authenticated rejected unavailable expired invalid } | 0828 §603.132 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6413 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Authorization: Authorization is capability-based by default. Role-based or attribute-based systems may be implemented above the primitive capability layer. | 0828 §603.133 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6414 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Role Mapping: An application may map: identity ↓ role ↓ capability set but the runtime should ultimately enforce concrete capabilities. | 0828 §603.134 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6415 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Session Identity: BOOTSTRAP-600 session state may expose: SessionIdentity for diagnostics and authorization. | 0828 §603.135 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6416 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Session Separation: Authentication credentials and session state must not be conflated. | 0828 §603.136 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6417 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Token Handling: Tokens should be represented as opaque types: AccessToken RefreshToken SessionToken rather than generic strings. | 0828 §603.137 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6418 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Token Logging: Token types are automatically protected from BOOTSTRAP-602 logging. | 0828 §603.138 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6419 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Token Equality: Security-sensitive token comparison uses constant-time comparison where applicable. | 0828 §603.139 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6420 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Expiration: Security credentials may expose: expires_at() without exposing secret contents. | 0828 §603.140 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6421 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Clock Security: Expiration checks should account for clock manipulation where the platform provides monotonic or trusted time sources. | 0828 §603.141 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6422 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Store: The runtime may provide access to platform trust stores through: TrustStore without exposing platform-specific internals. | 0828 §603.142 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6423 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Certificate Object: Certificates are parsed into typed structures. Malformed certificates return structured errors. | 0828 §603.143 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6424 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Certificate Validation: Validation may check: signature chain validity period key usage hostname policy revocation status depending on the requested operation. | 0828 §603.144 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6425 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hostname Validation: TLS-like network clients must not treat certificate-chain validity alone as hostname authorization. | 0828 §603.145 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6426 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — TLS Boundary: Axiom may provide secure network transports. The application API should make certificate and hostname validation the normal behavior. | 0828 §603.146 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6427 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plaintext Transport: Plaintext networking remains possible for explicitly non-sensitive protocols. Security-sensitive APIs should not silently downgrade to plaintext. | 0828 §603.147 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6428 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Downgrade Protection: A secure connection should not automatically downgrade after: certificate failure authentication failure protocol mismatch without an explicit application policy. | 0828 §603.148 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6429 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic Failure: Cryptographic verification failure must return a failure result. It must not be converted into a warning and continued silently. | 0828 §603.149 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6430 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Error Messages: Errors should explain enough for debugging without revealing secrets. Example: authentication failed rather than: password hash for user X was ... | 0828 §603.150 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6431 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Redaction: Security errors are automatically safe for BOOTSTRAP-602 diagnostic serialization. | 0828 §603.151 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6432 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Panic Safety: A security failure must not cause a panic merely because the capability was denied. | 0828 §603.152 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6433 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Privilege Boundary: Privilege escalation is represented explicitly: security.request_privilege(...) The runtime cannot silently elevate. | 0828 §603.153 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6434 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Privileged Helper: Some platforms may require a privileged helper process. The helper must have: minimal capability set authenticated IPC explicit protocol bounded input | 0828 §603.154 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6435 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Helper Authentication: The main process must authenticate the helper before sending sensitive operations. | 0828 §603.155 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6436 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Helper Authorization: The helper must authenticate the requesting application before accepting privileged operations. | 0828 §603.156 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6437 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Confused Deputy Prevention: A privileged helper must not blindly perform arbitrary operations requested by any client. Every request must be authorized against the caller's identity and granted capability. | 0828 §603.157 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6438 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Delegation: A process may delegate a restricted capability: parent ↓ child but delegation cannot exceed the parent's authority. | 0828 §603.158 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6439 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Child Process Security: When spawning a child process, the parent may specify: capabilities environment filesystem network handles working directory resource quotas | 0828 §603.159 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6440 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Default Child Authority: A child process receives no additional authority merely because the parent possesses it. | 0828 §603.160 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6441 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Inheritance: Inheritance must be explicit. Example: spawn(..., inherit = [.stdin, .stdout]) | 0828 §603.161 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6442 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Handle Inheritance: Native handle inheritance is disabled by default where platform semantics allow. | 0828 §603.162 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6443 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Temporary Capabilities: Some capabilities may have expiration: capability.until(deadline) | 0828 §603.163 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6444 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Time-Bounded Authority: After expiration: operation → denied | 0828 §603.164 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6445 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — One-Shot Capabilities: Some authority can be consumed once: OneShotCapability<T> Useful for: - secure handoff; - installation tokens; - one-time secrets. | 0828 §603.165 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6446 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Audit Identity: Every capability may have an opaque identifier for diagnostics: CapabilityId This identifier does not expose the capability's secret material. | 0828 §603.166 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6447 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Context: The runtime maintains a security context: SecurityContext { app_identity session_identity capabilities trust } | 0828 §603.167 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6448 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Context Propagation: Async tasks inherit only the security context explicitly configured for them. | 0828 §603.168 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6449 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Context Isolation: A child task may receive a reduced security context. | 0828 §603.169 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6450 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Ambient Privilege Leakage: A task created from a privileged context must not accidentally become globally privileged. | 0828 §603.170 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6451 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Thread Context: Thread-local storage may cache security context, but the authoritative capability state remains explicit and revocable. | 0828 §603.171 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6452 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — FFI Security Review Boundary: Any API declared: extern should identify whether it: reads files opens network executes code accesses devices uses credentials where this can be represented statically. | 0828 §603.172 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6453 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native Module Manifest: Native modules may declare: required_capabilities provided_capabilities security_level publisher | 0828 §603.173 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6454 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Module Loading Policy: The application may require: signed module approved publisher expected hash expected ABI expected version before loading. | 0828 §603.174 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6455 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — ABI Trust: ABI compatibility is distinct from security trust. A compatible module is not automatically a trusted module. | 0828 §603.175 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6456 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Update: The architecture supports signed application updates. Update process: download ↓ verify signature ↓ verify identity ↓ verify compatibility ↓ stage ↓ activate | 0828 §603.176 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6457 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Atomic Update: Where platform support exists, activation should be atomic. A failed update must leave the previous known-good installation intact. | 0828 §603.177 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6458 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Rollback: The deployment layer may maintain: current previous candidate versions. Security metadata must accompany each version. | 0828 §603.178 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6459 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Update Trust: A newer version must not automatically be trusted merely because it is newer. The signing/trust policy must still pass. | 0828 §603.179 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6460 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Bootstrap: At startup: platform ↓ executable identity ↓ signature/trust policy ↓ runtime initialization ↓ capability establishment ↓ application | 0828 §603.180 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6461 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Bootstrap Failure: If mandatory integrity verification fails: application startup = denied rather than continuing in a partially trusted state. | 0828 §603.181 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6462 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Integration: BOOTSTRAP-602 records: build ID publisher ID module identity capability denials trust failures security events but never raw secrets. | 0828 §603.182 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6463 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Integration: BOOTSTRAP-602 crash artifacts may contain: security context identifier trust status active capability class but not capability secrets. | 0828 §603.183 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6464 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Configuration Integration: BOOTSTRAP-601 declares requested capabilities. BOOTSTRAP-603 determines actual authority. | 0828 §603.184 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6465 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — State Integration: BOOTSTRAP-600 may persist: permission state security migration state session identity references but sensitive credentials remain in the secure credential subsystem. | 0828 §603.185 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6466 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Credential Persistence: Long-lived credentials should not be stored in ordinary BOOTSTRAP-600 application state. They belong to: secure storage platform credential store hardware-backed storage where available. | 0828 §603.186 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6467 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Storage API: secure_store.put(key, secret) secure_store.get(key) secure_store.delete(key) The storage provider may be platform-native. | 0828 §603.187 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6468 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Storage Provider: Possible providers: Windows credential facilities macOS Keychain iOS Keychain/Secure Enclave Android Keystore Linux secure store Axiom native encrypted store The API remains platform-neutral. | 0828 §603.188 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6469 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Software Fallback: Where no hardware secure store exists, the runtime may use software encryption. It must clearly distinguish: hardware-backed OS-backed software-protected storage. | 0828 §603.189 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6470 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Master Key: The runtime must not hard-code a universal master key. Keys derive from platform/user/application-specific secure sources. | 0828 §603.190 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6471 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Key Rotation: Secure storage supports versioned keys where practical. | 0828 §603.191 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6472 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Credential Deletion: Deleting a credential should invalidate its application reference. Best-effort physical erasure depends on the underlying storage technology. | 0828 §603.192 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6473 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Events: Recommended event IDs: SEC_CAPABILITY_DENIED SEC_CAPABILITY_REVOKED SEC_PERMISSION_CHANGED SEC_SIGNATURE_INVALID SEC_MODULE_REJECTED SEC_AUTH_FAILED SEC_CREDENTIAL_ACCESS SEC_TRUST_FAILED SEC_SANDBOX_VIOLATION SEC_QUOTA_EXCEEDED | 0828 §603.193 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6474 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Event Redaction: Security event payloads must pass through the same secret-protection layer as ordinary diagnostics. | 0828 §603.194 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6475 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Metrics: Optional counters: authorization_denied authentication_failed module_rejected capability_revoked sandbox_denied credential_failures | 0828 §603.195 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6476 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Health: SecurityHealth { trust_status sandbox_status secure_storage_status crypto_status } | 0828 §603.196 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6477 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Self-Test: Optional: security.self_test() may verify: - secure random source; - cryptographic backend; - secure storage; - capability subsystem; - trust metadata. It must not expose secrets. | 0828 §603.197 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6478 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Failure Isolation: If optional security telemetry fails: security enforcement continues Diagnostics must not weaken authorization merely because logging is unavailable. | 0828 §603.198 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6479 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fail-Closed Operations: For security-critical authorization: unknown must normally behave as: deny unless an explicitly documented policy says otherwise. | 0828 §603.199 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6480 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fail-Open Exceptions: Fail-open behavior must be explicitly declared and limited to operations where security consequences are acceptable. It must never be an accidental default. | 0828 §603.200 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6481 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Policy: Applications may define: SecurityPolicy { required_signer allowed_modules allowed_capabilities crypto_policy credential_policy } | 0828 §603.201 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6482 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Immutability: Once a security-critical policy is active, ordinary application code cannot silently weaken it. | 0828 §603.202 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6483 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Layers: Policy precedence: platform ↓ deployment ↓ application ↓ resource ↓ operation A lower layer may restrict authority but must not bypass a higher-level denial. | 0828 §603.203 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6484 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Policy Compilation: Static policy should be compiled into compact native structures where possible. | 0828 §603.204 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6485 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Runtime Cost: A capability authorization check should target: O(1) for ordinary capability operations. | 0828 §603.205 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6486 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Metadata: A release executable may contain: application identity publisher identity requested capabilities module requirements security policy hash | 0828 §603.206 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6487 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Fingerprint: The active security policy may expose: security.policy_fingerprint() This integrates with BOOTSTRAP-602 diagnostics. | 0828 §603.207 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6488 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Context Fingerprint: A diagnostic snapshot may contain: security policy fingerprint trust status capability profile without exposing individual secret values. | 0828 §603.208 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6489 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AI-Friendly Security Metadata: The toolchain should emit machine-readable metadata describing: capability requirements resource boundaries trust requirements module dependencies security policy This allows automated tooling to understand why an operation was denied. | 0828 §603.209 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6490 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Manifest: A deployment manifest should support: security: capabilities: trusted_publishers: trusted_modules: crypto_policy: sandbox: secure_storage: | 0828 §603.210 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6491 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Diff: Tooling should be able to compare two builds: build A capabilities vs build B capabilities and identify added/removed requested authority. | 0828 §603.211 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6492 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax security`: The toolchain should provide: ax security inspect ax security manifest ax security verify ax security capabilities ax security modules | 0828 §603.212 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6493 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax security capabilities`: Outputs: requested granted denied inherited delegated revoked | 0828 §603.213 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6494 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax security verify`: Checks: binary signature module signatures build identity manifest policy dependency integrity | 0828 §603.214 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6495 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Static Capability Analysis: The compiler may determine: function → required capability when capability requirements are explicit. Example: save_document() requires FileWrite | 0828 §603.215 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6496 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Propagation: If: fn save(cap: FileWriteCapability) calls: write_file(cap) the compiler can propagate the requirement. | 0828 §603.216 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6497 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Requirement Graph: The compiler may generate: function ↓ required capability ↓ module ↓ application manifest | 0828 §603.217 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6498 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dead Capability Elimination: If a capability-dependent subsystem is unused, associated runtime code should be removable. | 0828 §603.218 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6499 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Footprint: The toolchain should report: filesystem access network access process access device access credential access JIT access for an executable. | 0828 §603.219 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6500 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Footprint Does Not Equal Runtime Permission: Static analysis describes potential authority. The runtime determines actual granted authority. | 0828 §603.220 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6501 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Sandboxed Build: A build may intentionally restrict its static capability surface. The compiler can reject APIs requiring capabilities outside the declared profile. | 0828 §603.221 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6502 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Injection: At application startup: fn main( fs: FileSystemCapability, net: NetworkCapability ) may receive capabilities explicitly. This makes dependencies visible in the application entry point. | 0828 §603.222 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6503 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dependency Injection Without Framework: No dependency-injection framework is required. Capabilities are ordinary typed parameters. | 0828 §603.223 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6504 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Testing: Tests may inject mock capabilities: FakeFileSystemCapability provided they implement the required restricted interface. | 0828 §603.224 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6505 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Test Isolation: Tests should default to: no network no real credentials temporary filesystem no process spawning unless explicitly enabled. | 0828 §603.225 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6506 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Test Capability: The test runtime may expose synthetic capabilities that cannot affect the real system. | 0828 §603.226 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6507 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fuzzing: Security-sensitive parsers and capability boundaries should be fuzz-testable without requiring real privileged resources. | 0828 §603.227 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6508 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Deterministic Security Tests: Where practical, permission decisions should be testable deterministically. | 0828 §603.228 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6509 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Error Taxonomy: Core errors: SecurityError { denied unavailable expired revoked invalid_identity invalid_signature trust_failure quota_exceeded sandbox_violation credential_unavailable policy_violation } | 0828 §603.229 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6510 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Codes: Security errors have stable numeric IDs for diagnostics and IPC. | 0828 §603.230 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6511 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — ABI Stability: Security error and capability ABI structures require explicit versioning. | 0828 §603.231 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6512 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Platform Adapter Contract: Each platform adapter implements: identity permissions sandbox secure storage crypto randomness process authority filesystem authority network authority code trust where supported. | 0828 §603.232 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6513 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Windows Adapter: Integrates with: - process identity; - ACL/security descriptors; - code signing; - credential facilities; - protected storage where available; - native process/token mechanisms. | 0828 §603.233 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6514 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Linux Adapter: Integrates with: - file permissions; - user/group identity; - namespaces where available; - sandboxing mechanisms; - kernel credential boundaries; - native secure random source. | 0828 §603.234 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6515 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — macOS Adapter: Integrates with: - code signing; - entitlements; - sandbox; - Keychain; - application identity; - platform permission mechanisms. | 0828 §603.235 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6516 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — iOS Adapter: The architecture respects: - application sandbox; - entitlements; - Keychain; - Secure Enclave where available; - platform permission dialogs; - code-signing restrictions. | 0828 §603.236 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6517 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Android Adapter: Integrates with: - application identity; - permissions; - sandbox UID; - Keystore; - package signing; - platform security policy. | 0828 §603.237 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6518 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — WASM Adapter: WASM authority is determined by the host. Axiom capabilities map to host-provided imports/interfaces. No capability is assumed merely because the WASM module exists. | 0828 §603.238 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6519 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cross-Platform Semantic Rule: The same Axiom API should preserve this invariant: operation succeeds only if required capability is valid AND platform policy permits it | 0828 §603.239 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6520 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Platform Differences: The runtime may expose capability state as: supported unsupported restricted granted denied instead of pretending every platform provides identical security features. | 0828 §603.240 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6521 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No False Security: The runtime must not label software-only protection as hardware-backed protection. | 0828 §603.241 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6522 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Claims: Axiom documentation must distinguish: language guarantee runtime guarantee platform guarantee configuration guarantee best effort | 0828 §603.242 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6523 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Security: Security-sensitive memory APIs should provide: guarded allocation zeroization restricted access optional locking where supported. | 0828 §603.243 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6524 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Allocator: A secure allocator may exist: secure.alloc<T>(count) It is intended for sensitive data, not ordinary application allocations. | 0828 §603.244 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6525 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Allocator Constraints: Secure allocation may be: - slower; - non-movable; - non-swappable; - quota-limited. The application must opt in. | 0828 §603.245 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6526 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Universal Secure Memory Promise: The runtime cannot guarantee physical memory secrecy against a fully privileged operating system/kernel. Documentation must state the trust boundary. | 0828 §603.246 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6527 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Boundary: Default trust model: Application ↓ trusts Axiom runtime ↓ trusts Operating system ↓ trusts Hardware Platform security can alter this boundary. | 0828 §603.247 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6528 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hostile Application Code: The capability model assumes application components may be mutually untrusted. This enables future plugin/sandbox architectures. | 0828 §603.248 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6529 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plugin Capability Boundary: A plugin receives: only explicitly granted capabilities not the application's entire authority. | 0828 §603.249 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6530 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plugin Manifest: Plugins may declare: required capabilities publisher version hash ABI | 0828 §603.250 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6531 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plugin Approval: The host application determines whether the plugin is acceptable. The runtime enforces the granted capability boundary. | 0828 §603.251 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6532 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plugin Revocation: A plugin capability can be revoked without necessarily terminating the entire application. | 0828 §603.252 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6533 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Untrusted Data: External data is treated as: data not: trusted code until explicitly validated. | 0828 §603.253 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6534 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Conversion: Converting external data into privileged objects requires validation. | 0828 §603.254 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
