| REQ-ECO-6535 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Input Validation: The runtime provides primitives for: range checking length checking encoding validation schema validation signature validation | 0828 §603.255 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6536 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — UTF-8 Security: Axiom's UTF-8 default must not imply that arbitrary byte sequences are valid text. The runtime distinguishes: Bytes String | 0828 §603.256 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6537 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Invalid UTF-8: Converting bytes to String requires explicit validation or a defined lossy conversion. | 0828 §603.257 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6538 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unicode Normalization: Security-sensitive identifiers may optionally require normalization. The runtime must not silently normalize arbitrary user data. | 0828 §603.258 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6539 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Case Sensitivity: Security-sensitive resource names must respect platform-specific case semantics. The runtime should expose canonical comparison rules. | 0828 §603.259 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6540 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Filename Security: Applications must not assume: same textual path = same resource across platforms. Capability-bound resource handles remain authoritative. | 0828 §603.260 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6541 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Environment Security: BOOTSTRAP-601 environment values are untrusted input unless explicitly declared trusted. | 0828 §603.261 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6542 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Configuration Security: Configuration cannot grant itself capabilities beyond the deployment/platform policy. | 0828 §603.262 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6543 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — CLI Security: Command-line options cannot override mandatory security restrictions. | 0828 §603.263 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6544 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Debug Configuration: A debug flag cannot disable mandatory signature or sandbox enforcement in production. | 0828 §603.264 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6545 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Development Escape Hatch: Development-only bypasses must be: explicit visible build-identifiable non-default | 0828 §603.265 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6546 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Banner: Diagnostic metadata may identify: development security mode when enabled. | 0828 §603.266 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6547 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Production Build Validation: The build tool should warn or fail when production configuration contains: debug bypass trust-all disable-signature-check allow-unsigned-module style settings. | 0828 §603.267 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6548 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Policy Hash: The final executable may contain the hash of the security policy actually compiled into the binary. | 0828 §603.268 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6549 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Mismatch Detection: At startup: runtime policy vs deployment policy must be checked for compatibility. | 0828 §603.269 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6550 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Immutable Startup Security: Mandatory security decisions should occur before untrusted application initialization. | 0828 §603.270 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6551 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Early Attack Surface: The bootstrap sequence should minimize: dynamic loading network access configuration parsing plugin loading before security initialization. | 0828 §603.271 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6552 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Configuration Parsing: BOOTSTRAP-601 configuration files are untrusted input until validated. | 0828 §603.272 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6553 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Manifest Validation: The deployment manifest must be: parsed schema-checked policy-checked integrity-checked where applicable before capabilities are established. | 0828 §603.273 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6554 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Defaults on Parse Failure: Invalid security configuration results in: restricted startup rather than permissive fallback. | 0828 §603.274 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6555 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Startup Graph: Startup: identity ↓ trust verification ↓ manifest validation ↓ platform permissions ↓ capability construction ↓ application initialization | 0828 §603.275 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6556 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Shutdown: Shutdown invalidates or releases: temporary capabilities session credentials IPC channels privileged handles according to their lifecycle. | 0828 §603.276 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6557 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Session Termination: BOOTSTRAP-600 session termination must invalidate session-scoped capabilities. | 0828 §603.277 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6558 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User Logout: Where applicable: logout ↓ credential/session invalidation ↓ capability revocation | 0828 §603.278 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6559 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Event on Revocation: Capability revocation may generate: security.capability.revoked for diagnostics. | 0828 §603.279 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6560 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash-Time Security Capture: Crash handling may record: security policy fingerprint application identity publisher identity trust state but must not inspect all capabilities or credentials indiscriminately. | 0828 §603.280 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6561 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Diagnostics Boundary: BOOTSTRAP-603 owns: authority trust identity credential protection BOOTSTRAP-602 owns: recording diagnostic persistence crash reporting | 0828 §603.281 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6562 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Configuration Boundary: BOOTSTRAP-601 declares: desired deployment configuration BOOTSTRAP-603 decides: security authority actually available | 0828 §603.282 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6563 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and State Boundary: BOOTSTRAP-600 owns: application state BOOTSTRAP-603 owns: security state Only references to security state should enter ordinary application checkpoints. | 0828 §603.283 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6564 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security State: Security state may include: permission status capability revocation trust state credential references policy version | 0828 §603.284 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6565 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Credential References: Application state stores: CredentialId not: raw credential | 0828 §603.285 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6566 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Restore Safety: Restoring an application checkpoint must not automatically restore expired or revoked capabilities. | 0828 §603.286 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6567 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security-Aware Recovery: After crash recovery: application state restored + security state revalidated before privileged operations resume. | 0828 §603.287 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6568 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Replay Protection: Security-sensitive operations must not be replayed merely because application state was restored. | 0828 §603.288 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6569 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Transaction Identity: Security-sensitive transactions may include: TransactionId Nonce SessionId for replay protection. | 0828 §603.289 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6570 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Monotonic Counter: Platforms supporting secure counters may expose them through: secure.counter() for replay-sensitive applications. | 0828 §603.290 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6571 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Atomic Security State: Permission/capability changes should be applied atomically from the application's perspective. | 0828 §603.291 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6572 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Concurrent Revocation: If a capability is revoked concurrently with an operation, the runtime defines whether: operation already authorized may complete. The default rule is: > Revocation prevents subsequent authorization; it does not necessarily cancel an already-authorized kernel operation. | 0828 §603.292 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6573 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Authorization Race: Security-sensitive operations should use atomic platform primitives where available to reduce authorization races. | 0828 §603.293 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6574 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Invariant: At all times: effective authority ⊆ granted authority ⊆ deployment authority ⊆ platform authority | 0828 §603.294 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6575 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Privilege Amplification: No combination of ordinary Axiom APIs may transform: Capability<A> into: Capability<UnrelatedPrivilege> without an explicit trusted boundary. | 0828 §603.295 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6576 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Monotonicity: Capability derivation must satisfy: Authority(child) <= Authority(parent) unless the operation crosses a separately authenticated privilege boundary. | 0828 §603.296 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6577 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Boundary Crossing: Crossing into a privileged subsystem requires: authentication authorization input validation bounded resource use audit event where applicable. | 0828 §603.297 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6578 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Ambient Root Capability: Axiom does not expose: root_capability() to ordinary application code. | 0828 §603.298 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6579 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trusted Runtime Code: Some runtime operations necessarily require elevated native authority. These are isolated inside trusted runtime components. | 0828 §603.299 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6580 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trusted Runtime Surface: The trusted computing base should be kept small. Optional subsystems should remain outside the mandatory security core. | 0828 §603.300 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6581 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compiler Trust: The compiler is part of the build-time trust boundary. Reproducible builds and signed compiler/toolchain artifacts are outside the mandatory application runtime but supported by the ecosystem. | 0828 §603.301 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6582 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Self-Identity: The runtime exposes: runtime.identity() including: runtime version ABI build identity security feature set | 0828 §603.302 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6583 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Feature Availability: Applications can query: security.features() to determine platform support. | 0828 §603.303 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6584 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Introspection: Applications may inspect whether a capability is: valid revoked expired restricted but should not be able to extract privileged internal representation. | 0828 §603.304 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6585 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Handle Introspection: A `Handle<T>` should expose only safe metadata: valid type state not raw kernel pointers unless explicitly requested through an unsafe API. | 0828 §603.305 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6586 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unsafe Native Handle Extraction: If required for FFI: unsafe native_handle(handle) must be explicitly marked unsafe. | 0828 §603.306 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6587 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native Handle Lifetime: The developer is responsible for respecting the ownership contract when using extracted handles. | 0828 §603.307 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6588 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Memory Model: The security architecture must remain compatible with Axiom's high-performance native memory model. It must not introduce: - mandatory GC; - mandatory borrow checker; - mandatory reference counting; - hidden heap allocations. | 0828 §603.308 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6589 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Performance: Security checks should use: typed capabilities opaque handles constant-time primitives where required bounded authorization checks rather than pervasive dynamic policy interpretation. | 0828 §603.309 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6590 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fast Path: After capability validation, hot resource operations may use a compact validated handle. Example: Capability ↓ validate NativeHandle ↓ fast operation | 0828 §603.310 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6591 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Revocation Tradeoff: Instant revocation may require indirection. The runtime may choose: generation counter capability table revocation epoch kernel-backed handle depending on platform. | 0828 §603.311 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6592 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Generation Counters: A capability handle may encode: index generation so stale handles are rejected. | 0828 §603.312 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6593 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Stale Capability: Using a stale capability returns: SecurityError.revoked rather than accessing a reused resource. | 0828 §603.313 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6594 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Resource Identity: The runtime should distinguish: resource identity handle identity capability identity | 0828 §603.314 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6595 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Table: A runtime implementation may maintain: CapabilityTable for resources requiring centralized revocation. | 0828 §603.315 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6596 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Table Performance: Lookup target: O(1) average case. | 0828 §603.316 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6597 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Table Memory: Entries are bounded by configured resource limits. | 0828 §603.317 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6598 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Resource Exhaustion: Failure to create a capability due to table exhaustion returns: SecurityError.quota_exceeded or an explicit resource-exhaustion error. | 0828 §603.318 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6599 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Telemetry: Security metrics must not become an attack vector. High-volume security failures must be rate-limited. | 0828 §603.319 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6600 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Event Flood: If an attacker causes thousands of permission failures: application remains responsive and diagnostic storage remains bounded. | 0828 §603.320 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6601 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Logging Priority: Critical security events may bypass ordinary log filtering while still respecting privacy. | 0828 §603.321 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6602 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Durability: Applications requiring durable security auditing can configure durable storage explicitly. Ordinary application logs do not receive this guarantee automatically. | 0828 §603.322 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6603 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Tamper Evidence: Optional hash chaining: H0 H1 = H(H0 // E1) H2 = H(H1 // E2) ... allows detection of modifications. | 0828 §603.323 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6604 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Key: Tamper-evident audit chains may use a signing key or MAC key stored through secure storage. | 0828 §603.324 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6605 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Verification: Tool: ax security audit verify checks chain integrity. | 0828 §603.325 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6606 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Export: Audit export must preserve: event identity timestamp sequence integrity metadata | 0828 §603.326 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6607 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Automatic Remote Upload: Security audit data is never automatically uploaded by the core runtime. | 0828 §603.327 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6608 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Threat Model: The implementation specification must explicitly document whether it protects against: untrusted application input untrusted plugins untrusted local users malicious modules network attackers compromised dependencies | 0828 §603.328 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6609 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Out of Scope Threats: The core runtime cannot guarantee protection against: fully compromised operating system fully compromised kernel malicious hypervisor physically compromised hardware unless platform-specific trusted hardware establishes such a boundary. | 0828 §603.329 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6610 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Threat Model Metadata: Build documentation may contain: security assumptions trust boundaries platform requirements | 0828 §603.330 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6611 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Review Artifact: The toolchain may generate: .axsecurity containing: capability graph module trust graph security policy resource permissions crypto usage | 0828 §603.331 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6612 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AI Security Analysis: An AI tool can consume `.axsecurity` to answer: Which function requires network access? Which module can access credentials? Which plugin has filesystem write authority? Which build gained a new capability? without inspecting every source file. | 0828 §603.332 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6613 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Diff: The tool should support: ax security diff old.axsecurity new.axsecurity and identify structural changes. The tool reports facts; it does not assign a security score. | 0828 §603.333 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6614 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compiler Diagnostics: Examples: SEC001 capability required SEC002 capability unavailable SEC003 secret passed to diagnostic API SEC004 unsigned module SEC005 invalid trust policy SEC006 insecure random source SEC007 unsafe credential conversion SEC008 forbidden privilege escalation SEC009 invalid capability attenuation SEC010 security policy mismatch | 0828 §603.334 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6615 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compile-Time Secret Protection: The compiler should reject obvious flows: Secret<T> ↓ String ↓ log() unless explicitly overridden through an unsafe security API. | 0828 §603.335 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6616 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Static Taint Metadata: The compiler may track: secret untrusted trusted privileged metadata. This is optional but strongly supported. | 0828 §603.336 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6617 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Untrusted Data: External input may be marked: Untrusted<T> and validated into: Trusted<T> when a validator succeeds. | 0828 §603.337 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6618 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trusted Conversion: Example: let username = validate_username(input)? returns a restricted validated type. | 0828 §603.338 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6619 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Taint Propagation: The compiler may propagate security metadata through: assignment function parameters struct fields serialization FFI logging | 0828 §603.339 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6620 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Taint Does Not Replace Authorization: A value being marked `Trusted<T>` does not grant resource capabilities. | 0828 §603.340 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6621 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Metadata Cost: Security metadata should be erased from runtime representations whenever it is compile-time-only. | 0828 §603.341 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6622 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Zero Runtime Cost Security Types: Where possible: Trusted<T> Untrusted<T> Secret<T> should have the same physical representation as `T`, while enforcing restrictions through the compiler. | 0828 §603.342 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6623 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Secret Protection: Runtime protection remains necessary when secrets cross dynamic/native boundaries. | 0828 §603.343 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6624 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Serialization: Secrets cannot be serialized through generic serializers without an explicit security policy. | 0828 §603.344 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6625 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Persistence: `Secret<T>` does not imply persistence. Secure storage is a separate subsystem. | 0828 §603.345 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6626 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Delete: Secure deletion semantics are platform-dependent. The API must distinguish: logical delete best-effort overwrite secure-store destruction | 0828 §603.346 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6627 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No False Erasure Guarantee: Axiom must not promise physical deletion on storage systems where the underlying medium cannot provide it. | 0828 §603.347 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6628 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Serialization: Capabilities generally cannot be serialized directly. Instead: capability ↓ explicit transferable token may be used. | 0828 §603.348 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6629 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Token: Transfer tokens must be: opaque bounded expiring where appropriate single-use where appropriate | 0828 §603.349 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6630 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Token Binding: A transfer token may be bound to: recipient identity session process resource expiration | 0828 §603.350 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6631 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Replay Prevention: Single-use security tokens must contain replay-protection state. | 0828 §603.351 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6632 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure IPC Token Exchange: Token exchange: sender ↓ authenticate receiver ↓ verify token ↓ construct capability | 0828 §603.352 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6633 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Delegation Graph: The runtime may represent: root capability ↓ attenuated capability ↓ delegated capability for audit purposes. | 0828 §603.353 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6634 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Delegation Constraint: Delegated authority cannot exceed the authority of the delegating capability. | 0828 §603.354 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6635 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Context Snapshot: A diagnostic snapshot may record the identity of the security context but not its secret internal representation. | 0828 §603.355 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6636 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Context Recovery: After process restart, capability objects are recreated from platform authorization rather than blindly restored from serialized memory. | 0828 §603.356 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6637 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Recovery Security Rule: A restored application checkpoint cannot resurrect: revoked permission expired credential expired capability invalid trust state | 0828 §603.357 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6638 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Application Update Security: State migration across versions must not automatically transfer obsolete privileged capabilities. | 0828 §603.358 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6639 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Migration: When an application updates: old capability model ↓ policy reconciliation ↓ new capability model | 0828 §603.359 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6640 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Version: Security policy has a version identifier. | 0828 §603.360 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6641 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Migration: Breaking security-policy changes require explicit migration logic. | 0828 §603.361 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6642 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Defaults During Migration: If migration fails: restricted mode rather than unrestricted mode. | 0828 §603.362 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6643 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Emergency Recovery: Applications may expose a recovery mode with minimal authority: read diagnostics repair configuration restore state but no unnecessary network/process/device authority. | 0828 §603.363 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6644 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Recovery Capability: Recovery mode receives a deliberately reduced capability set. | 0828 §603.364 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6645 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Safe Mode: Axiom may provide: application.safe_mode() at the lifecycle layer. BOOTSTRAP-603 supplies the security profile. | 0828 §603.365 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6646 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Safe Mode Diagnostics: Safe mode integrates with BOOTSTRAP-602 so that security failures remain diagnosable. | 0828 §603.366 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6647 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Platform Permission Prompt: Axiom must not bypass platform permission dialogs. | 0828 §603.367 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6648 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission UX: User-facing permission explanations belong to the application/UI layer. The security runtime exposes machine-readable permission reasons. | 0828 §603.368 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6649 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission Reason: Example: PermissionReason.camera.capture | 0828 §603.369 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6650 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission Minimization: The compiler/toolchain should be able to determine which declared capabilities are actually referenced. | 0828 §603.370 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6651 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unused Capability Warning: If a manifest requests a capability never used by the executable: warning: unused capability request | 0828 §603.371 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6652 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Reduction: The deployment tool may generate a minimized manifest containing only required capabilities. | 0828 §603.372 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6653 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic Capability Use: Dynamic plugins may prevent complete static capability analysis. The tool must mark such requirements as dynamic rather than pretending certainty. | 0828 §603.373 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6654 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic Loading Warning: Applications using unrestricted dynamic module discovery should receive an explicit security diagnostic. | 0828 §603.374 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6655 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Boundary Documentation: Every native platform adapter must document: what it guarantees what it delegates what it cannot guarantee | 0828 §603.375 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6656 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cross-Compilation: Security metadata must remain valid when targeting another platform. | 0828 §603.376 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6657 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unsupported Capability: When a target lacks a capability: compile-time error if required statically, or: unsupported at runtime if dynamically optional. | 0828 §603.377 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6658 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Silent Emulation: A capability must not silently degrade into a weaker security mechanism. | 0828 §603.378 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6659 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crypto Backend: Axiom may have a native crypto backend selected per target. The public API remains stable. | 0828 §603.379 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6660 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Backend Independence: Applications should not depend directly on the internal cryptographic implementation. | 0828 §603.380 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6661 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Constant-Time Native Primitives: Security-critical primitive implementations should avoid data-dependent branches where algorithmically required. | 0828 §603.381 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6662 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Side-Channel Documentation: The runtime documentation must state which side-channel protections are guaranteed and which depend on the platform. | 0828 §603.382 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6663 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hardware Acceleration: Crypto operations may use: CPU instructions hardware security modules platform crypto APIs without changing the public API. | 0828 §603.383 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6664 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — CPU Feature Detection: The runtime may select accelerated crypto implementations after securely determining CPU features. | 0828 §603.384 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6665 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Unsafe Fallback: A hardware-accelerated implementation may fall back to a compatible software implementation, but not to an insecure algorithm merely because acceleration is unavailable. | 0828 §603.385 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6666 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Entropy Failure: If secure randomness is unavailable: secure.random() must fail. It must not silently fall back to predictable randomness. | 0828 §603.386 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6667 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Time: Security protocols requiring trusted time should use platform facilities where available. | 0828 §603.387 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6668 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Time-Based Authorization: Expiration checks must define behavior if the system clock moves backward or forward unexpectedly. | 0828 §603.388 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6669 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Monotonic Expiration: Where practical, short-lived capabilities should use monotonic deadlines. | 0828 §603.389 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6670 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Performance Target: Capability checks should target: O(1) and minimal allocations. | 0828 §603.390 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6671 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic Performance: The runtime should expose hardware-accelerated implementations where available without changing semantics. | 0828 §603.391 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6672 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Binary Size: Unused cryptographic algorithms and security providers should be dead-strippable. | 0828 §603.392 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6673 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Minimal Security Runtime: A minimal native application should be able to include only: identity capability core secure randomness required platform security without pulling the entire diagnostics/security ecosystem. | 0828 §603.393 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6674 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory GC: Security types must not require garbage collection. | 0828 §603.394 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6675 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory Reference Counting: Security handles use deterministic ownership/lifetime semantics. Reference counting may be used internally where useful but is not a language requirement. | 0828 §603.395 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6676 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory Borrow Checker: Capability safety is achieved through: opaque types ownership capability construction rules runtime validation rather than requiring a universal borrow-checking model. | 0828 §603.396 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6677 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Flat Memory: The security subsystem remains compatible with Axiom's native memory architecture. Privileged resources remain represented as opaque handles rather than exposing raw security-sensitive memory addresses. | 0828 §603.397 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6678 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Struct-Oriented Design: Security abstractions use structs/traits rather than mandatory classes. Example: struct FileCapability { handle: Handle<FileAuthority> } fn read(cap: FileCapability, path: Path) | 0828 §603.398 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6679 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Override Compatibility: Platform-specific security adapters may override trait implementations without introducing class inheritance. | 0828 §603.399 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6680 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Trait Example: trait Capability { fn is_valid(self) -> bool fn revoke(self) } Concrete platform types implement the trait. | 0828 §603.400 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |

| REQ-ECO-6682 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compile-Time Security Graph: The compiler may construct: module ↓ function ↓ capability ↓ resource graphs. | 0828 §603.402 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |

| REQ-ECO-6685 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Acceptance Criteria: BOOTSTRAP-603 is complete when the Axiom implementation demonstrates: ### Capability - typed capabilities; - non-forgeable privileged authority; - attenuation; - revocation; - expiration; - delegation; - quotas; - explicit inheritance. ### Identity - application identity; - build identity; - publisher identity; - module identity; - peer identity. ### Trust - signature verification; - module verification; - policy enforcement; - trust-state reporting. ### Secrets - opaque secret types; - secure storage; - zeroization; - secret-safe diagnostics; - hardware-backed integration where available. ### Cryptography - secure random; - hashes; - MAC; - KDF; - AEAD; - signatures; - typed keys; - constant-time comparison. ### Platform - Windows; - Linux; - macOS; - iOS; - Android; - WASM. ### Isolation - sandbox integration; - process capability; - filesystem capability; - network capability; - device capability; - IPC capability. ### Compiler - static capability analysis; - capability metadata; - security diagnostics; - capability dead stripping; - AI-readable security graph. ### Runtime - O(1)-target authorization; - no mandatory GC; - no mandatory borrow checker; - deterministic resource cleanup; - bounded security metadata. | 0828 §603.405 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6686 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required Compiler/Runtime Components: Logical components: axiom.security.core axiom.security.capability axiom.security.identity axiom.security.trust axiom.security.crypto axiom.security.secrets axiom.security.storage axiom.security.ipc axiom.security.sandbox axiom.security.audit They need not become separate binaries. | 0828 §603.406 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6687 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required Tooling: The Axiom toolchain should provide: ax security inspect ax security verify ax security capabilities ax security diff ax security audit ax security modules | 0828 §603.407 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6688 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Artifact: The toolchain should generate: .axsecurity containing machine-readable: capability graph identity trust requirements module graph policy crypto usage security boundaries | 0828 §603.408 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6689 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AI-Agent Consumption: An AI coding agent should be able to inspect `.axsecurity` and determine: why an API requires authority which module owns that authority which caller supplied it whether a capability is static or dynamic which deployment permission is missing without scanning the complete source tree. | 0828 §603.409 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6690 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Architecture Invariants: The following invariants are mandatory: 1. Authority is explicit. 2. Authority cannot increase through attenuation. 3. Privileged capabilities cannot be forged by ordinary code. 4. Unknown security state fails closed by default. 5. Secrets cannot enter ordinary diagnostics accidentally. 6. Revoked authority cannot be used for new operations. 7. Restored state cannot resurrect revoked authority. 8. Dynamic modules do not automatically become trusted. 9. Secure randomness never silently falls back to predictable randomness. 10. Security failures cannot silently downgrade to insecure behavior. 11. Security enforcement does not depend on diagnostics availability. 12. Security metadata does not require GC. 13. Platform differences remain explicit. 14. The application cannot grant itself platform authority. 15. The runtime does not require a third-party security service. | 0828 §603.410 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6691 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Architectural Result: After BOOTSTRAP-603, the Axiom native runtime has the following security foundation: APPLICATION │ ┌───────┴───────┐ ▼               ▼ IDENTITY         STATE 600 │ ▼ TRUST │ ▼ CAPABILITY CORE ┌──────┼──────┐ ▼      ▼      ▼ FILE    NETWORK  IPC │      │      │ └──────┼──────┘ ▼ SECURE HANDLES │ ┌─────────┼─────────┐ ▼         ▼         ▼ CRYPTO    SECRETS   SANDBOX │         │         │ └─────────┼─────────┘ ▼ SECURITY AUDIT │ ▼ BOOTSTRAP-602 The three preceding bootstrap layers now form a coherent native application foundation: 600 = state / session / recovery 601 = configuration / environment / deployment 602 = diagnostics / crash / observability 603 = identity / authority / trust / security | 0828 §603.411 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6692 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Task Completion: **BOOTSTRAP-603 is complete.** The specification establishes: - capability-based security; - explicit authority; - capability attenuation; - capability revocation; - identity and trust; - secure handles; - secure storage; - secret protection; - cryptographic primitives; - secure randomness; - sandbox integration; - IPC security; - module trust; - code-signing integration; - privilege separation; - child-process security; - secure update foundations; - static capability analysis; - AI-readable security metadata; - platform-specific security adapters; - deterministic resource ownership; - compatibility with Axiom's native/high-performance memory model; - no mandatory GC; - no mandatory borrow checker; - no mandatory third-party security runtime. **Next task: `BOOTSTRAP-604 — NATIVE APPLICATION RESOURCE, MEMORY, CPU, GPU & ENERGY GOVERNANCE RUNTIME 5.0`** .: | 0828 §603.412 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-6693 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Mục tiêu: BOOTSTRAP-602 định nghĩa hệ thống: - structured logging; - diagnostics; - tracing; - metrics; - health/status; - crash handling; - panic/fatal error reporting; - native stack capture; - crash artifact; - minidump/core-dump abstraction; - symbolization; - diagnostic context; - correlation ID; - bounded diagnostic buffers; - crash-safe emergency logging; - log rotation; - diagnostic redaction; - build/config/state correlation; - local và production observability. Mục tiêu chính: > Một ứng dụng Axiom native phải có khả năng tự quan sát, tự chẩn đoán và tạo artifact đủ để điều tra lỗi mà không bắt buộc phụ thuộc vào một logging/telemetry framework bên thứ ba. | REQ-ECO-7193 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Core invariant summary: BOOTSTRAP-602 phải bảo đảm: 1. Logging is structured. 2. Disabled logging is near-zero cost. 3. Diagnostic memory is bounded. 4. Platform differences are isolated behind native backends. 13. Runtime can degrade gracefully. 14. Diagnostic failures do not normally crash the application. 15. Full observability can be stripped from minimal binaries. | 0829 §602.500 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |

| REQ-ECO-7711 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Mục tiêu: BOOTSTRAP-603 định nghĩa security foundation của Axiom native runtime. Subsystem phải cung cấp: 1. Security boundary. 2. Capability-based access control. 3. Permission model. 4. Privilege separation. 5. Resource authority. 6. Process/module trust boundaries. 7. Sandboxing integration. 8. Secret access control. 9. File/network/device capabilities. 10. Native OS permission mapping. 11. Runtime capability attenuation. 12. Secure defaults. 13. Explicit privilege escalation. 14. Capability inspection. 15. Audit integration. 16. Secure IPC boundary. 17. Plugin/module isolation. 18. Crash-safe security behavior. 19. Compiler/linker security metadata. 20. Minimal overhead when security features are unused. Core principle: > **Code chỉ có quyền làm những gì capability của nó cho phép.** | 0831 §603.0 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |

| REQ-ECO-8049 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission persistence: Persistence semantics delegated to OS/deployment. | 0831 §603.338 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8050 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Mobile lifecycle: When application backgrounded/suspended, capabilities may become temporarily unusable. Operations must handle OS denial. | 0831 §603.339 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8051 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability status: Status can be: active temporarily_unavailable revoked denied | 0831 §603.340 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8052 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — WASM host capability: Host provides explicit imports. Axiom runtime cannot access host resources not imported. | 0831 §603.341 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8053 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — WASM sandbox invariant: WASM linear memory does not imply host filesystem/network authority. | 0831 §603.342 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8054 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native sandbox: Native sandbox policy must be queried at startup. | 0831 §603.343 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8055 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security bootstrap report: Startup diagnostics can record: security profile sandbox type policy fingerprint granted capability count | 0831 §603.344 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8056 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No capability value logging: Never output actual capability token internals. | 0831 §603.345 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8057 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability leak prevention: Capability objects should not implement generic string serialization. | 0831 §603.346 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8058 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Generic serialization restriction: Compiler rejects serialization of capability types unless explicit safe projection exists. | 0831 §603.347 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8059 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Equality semantics: Capability equality means: same authority/resource identity not token byte equality exposed to application. | 0831 §603.348 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8060 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hash semantics: Capability can be hashable only through stable opaque identity. | 0831 §603.349 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8061 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Ordering: Capabilities do not have meaningful ordering. | 0831 §603.350 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8062 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability type system: Each capability kind is distinct at compile time. | 0831 §603.351 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8063 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Generic capability constraints: Functions may accept: fn read<T: ReadCapability>(cap: T) if useful. | 0831 §603.352 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8064 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability traits: Traits can describe: Readable Writable Connectable Delegatable Revocable | 0831 §603.353 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8065 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trait semantics: Capability trait does not grant authority. It describes operations supported by an already-authorized capability. | 0831 §603.354 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8066 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Struct-only integration: Capability objects are ordinary Axiom structs with runtime-managed opaque handles. No class hierarchy required. | 0831 §603.355 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8067 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Method integration: Methods: fn read(self: FileRead, ...) follow Axiom struct-first method convention. | 0831 §603.356 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8068 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Override integration: Platform-specific capability implementations can override behavior through trait/function dispatch without requiring classes. | 0831 §603.357 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8069 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic dispatch: Security-critical dispatch must not rely on mutable user-controlled vtables. | 0831 §603.358 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8070 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Static dispatch preference: Compile-time known capability operations should prefer static dispatch. | 0831 §603.359 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8071 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security metadata and generics: Generic functions must preserve capability requirements after monomorphization/specialization. | 0831 §603.360 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8072 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability requirements in IR: Compiler IR includes: requires_capability acquire_capability attenuate_capability release_capability where needed. | 0831 §603.361 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8073 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — IR validation: IR verifier must reject invalid capability operations: forge upgrade use-after-drop wrong-kind | 0831 §603.362 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8074 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Linker security verification: Linker validates final capability metadata against object/module metadata. | 0831 §603.363 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8075 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Loader verification: Native loader/runtime verifies signed/trusted module metadata before granting privileged capabilities where configured. | 0831 §603.364 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8076 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime module quarantine: Untrusted dynamic module may load into isolated process instead of same process. | 0831 §603.365 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8077 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security policy compiler output: Compact policy: .cap or equivalent. Exact extension remains implementation detail. | 0831 §603.366 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8078 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy format version: Security policy format must be versioned independently from application config. | 0831 §603.367 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8079 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy parser security: Parser must be: bounded non-executable deterministic | 0831 §603.368 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8080 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No policy scripting: Core security policy must not execute arbitrary user scripts. | 0831 §603.369 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8081 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy expressions: Keep policy language declarative: allow capability X scope resource Y deny operation Z | 0831 §603.370 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8082 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No arbitrary code in policy: Policy evaluation cannot call application functions. | 0831 §603.371 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8083 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy complexity: Avoid general-purpose rule engines in runtime. | 0831 §603.372 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8084 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fast path: Common decision: capability handle valid + resource within scope + operation allowed → direct allow. | 0831 §603.373 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8085 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Slow path: Only complex cases use policy engine. | 0831 §603.374 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8086 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security startup cost: Startup policy compilation should be O(policy size). | 0831 §603.375 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8087 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime check complexity: Common resource checks should be O(1) or bounded. | 0831 §603.376 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8088 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory footprint: Security runtime should use: immutable policy snapshot capability table small generation state rather than heavyweight object graphs. | 0831 §603.377 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8089 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No GC dependency: Security subsystem must not require garbage collection. | 0831 §603.378 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8090 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory safety: Capability implementation must obey Axiom memory model and cannot depend on GC or borrow checker. | 0831 §603.379 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8091 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Handle safety: Generation/index validation provides use-after-free protection for runtime-managed capability handles. | 0831 §603.380 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8092 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Integer overflow: Capability/resource calculations must use checked arithmetic where overflow can affect security. | 0831 §603.381 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8093 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Canonical resource IDs: Resources should use canonical identifiers to avoid alternate-path authorization bypasses. | 0831 §603.382 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8094 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — File case sensitivity: Path security adapter must respect platform case semantics. | 0831 §603.383 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8095 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unicode normalization: Filesystem/network identifiers requiring canonicalization must define Unicode normalization policy per platform. | 0831 §603.384 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8096 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Homograph handling: Security policy should avoid relying on human-readable names as identity. | 0831 §603.385 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8097 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — DNS security: Network authorization should account for DNS resolution changes if policy is hostname-based. | 0831 §603.386 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8098 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hostname capability semantics: If capability says: api.example.com implementation must define whether authority follows: hostname resolved IP both | 0831 §603.387 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8099 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — TLS: TLS authentication belongs to network/security libraries, while capability controls network authority. | 0831 §603.388 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8100 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Certificate authority: Certificate trust configuration is separate from capability grant. | 0831 §603.389 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8101 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Network identity distinction: NetworkConnect does not imply: trusted server | 0831 §603.390 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8102 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — File identity distinction: FileRead does not imply: file contents are trusted | 0831 §603.391 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8103 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Device identity distinction: DeviceAccess does not imply device data is safe. | 0831 §603.392 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8104 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust boundary input validation: Capability grants access; parser validation still required. | 0831 §603.393 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8105 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security architecture invariant: authority != trustworthiness of data | 0831 §603.394 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8106 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and diagnostics: BOOTSTRAP-602 records security decisions. BOOTSTRAP-603 decides authorization. | 0831 §603.395 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8107 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and config: BOOTSTRAP-601 provides policy inputs. BOOTSTRAP-603 validates/executes them. | 0831 §603.396 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8108 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and state: BOOTSTRAP-600 persists application state, never live privilege state. | 0831 §603.397 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8109 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and compiler: Compiler proves/records declared authority requirements. Runtime enforces actual authority. | 0831 §603.398 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8110 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and OS: OS remains final authority for kernel-protected resources. Axiom cannot grant more than OS allows. | 0831 §603.399 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8111 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security core invariant: The complete authority chain is: OS authority ↓ deployment policy ↓ Axiom security policy ↓ capability ↓ operation A lower layer cannot increase authority beyond the upper boundary. | 0831 §603.400 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8112 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required implementation phases: ### Phase 1 — Capability primitives Capability<T> generation opaque handle attenuation drop ### Phase 2 — Filesystem/network FileRead FileWrite NetworkConnect NetworkListen ### Phase 3 — Process/IPC ProcessSpawn ProcessDebug IPC SharedMemory ### Phase 4 — Compiler integration @requires capability metadata IR validation linker merge ### Phase 5 — Platform integration Windows Linux macOS iOS Android WASM ### Phase 6 — Sandboxing/trust plugin isolation module trust signature verification policy enforcement ### Phase 7 — Advanced security revocation quotas audit policy reload security tooling | 0831 §603.401 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8113 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required tests: At minimum: capability forgery wrong capability type stale handle revoked handle attenuation escape path traversal symlink escape network scope violation process privilege violation IPC unauthorized request plugin overreach FFI boundary policy reload policy corruption secret leakage concurrent revoke/use | 0831 §603.402 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8114 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cross-platform acceptance: Required targets: Windows x64 Linux x64 Linux ARM64 macOS ARM64 iOS ARM64 Android ARM64 WASM Unsupported platform capability must return: NotSupported not silently grant access. | 0831 §603.403 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8115 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Performance acceptance: Common authorized operation must not require: string permission lookup global mutex dynamic policy parsing on every call. | 0831 §603.404 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8116 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Binary-size acceptance: Applications that do not use advanced security capabilities should not pull: policy compiler plugin verifier signature subsystem advanced audit into the final binary unnecessarily. | 0831 §603.405 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8117 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security acceptance: Must prove: no capability forgery no authority escalation through attenuation no stale capability reuse no policy-cache bypass no partial policy reload no secret serialization no silent fail-open | 0831 §603.406 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8118 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Developer experience acceptance: Simple application: fn main(caps: AppCapabilities) { let file = caps.data.read("hello.txt") print(file) } should not require developers to understand the complete security engine. | 0831 §603.407 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8119 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Advanced developer experience: Security-sensitive server: fn run(caps: ServerCapabilities) { let listener = caps.network.listen(443) spawn(worker, with = [ caps.data.read_only() ]) } should make authority explicit and easy to audit. | 0831 §603.408 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8120 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Final architectural principle: Axiom security should follow: > **Explicit authority, least privilege, monotonic attenuation, fail-closed enforcement, platform-native isolation, and negligible overhead when unused.** | 0831 §603.409 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8121 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — BOOTSTRAP-603 completion invariant: BOOTSTRAP-603 is complete at architecture level when: capability model + permission model + policy engine + resource scoping + privilege separation + sandbox integration + IPC security + module/plugin trust + secret integration + compiler metadata + IR enforcement + linker validation + runtime enforcement + OS adapters + audit integration + revocation + resource limits + security testing đã được định nghĩa đủ để triển khai compiler/runtime mà không cần thiết kế lại security foundation. | 0831 §603.410 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8122 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Mục tiêu: Axiom cần một IPC runtime thống nhất để các process có thể: - gửi message; - gọi request/response; - truyền stream; - truyền buffer lớn; - chia sẻ memory; - truyền OS handle; - truyền capability; - phát event; - phát hiện peer chết; - timeout/cancel; - reconnect; - kiểm soát backpressure; - xác thực peer; - kiểm soát quyền truy cập. IPC phải hoạt động trên: - Windows; - Linux; - macOS; - Android; - iOS; - WASM/WASI ở mức capability phù hợp; - embedded target nếu platform adapter cung cấp primitive tương ứng. IPC core **không được phụ thuộc vào TCP/IP**. IPC mạng và distributed networking là lớp khác. | 0832 §604.0 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8123 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Nguyên tắc kiến trúc: Axiom IPC được chia thành các lớp: Application ↓ Service / RPC API ↓ Message API ↓ Transport ↓ OS IPC Primitive Shared memory đi theo nhánh: Application ↓ SharedBuffer / SharedRegion ↓ SharedMemory Transport ↓ OS Shared Memory Primitive Security: BOOTSTRAP-603 ↓ Capability ↓ Endpoint authorization ↓ Message / shared-memory operation Diagnostics: BOOTSTRAP-602 ↓ IPC trace / metrics / faults State: BOOTSTRAP-600 ↓ checkpoint / recovery integration Configuration: BOOTSTRAP-601 ↓ endpoint / limits / policy configuration | 0832 §604.1 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8124 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — IPC không phải distributed system: Core IPC chỉ đảm bảo semantics trong phạm vi mà transport hỗ trợ. Axiom không tuyên bố: - exactly-once delivery; - distributed transactions; - consensus; - distributed locks; - global ordering; - network reliability. Những chức năng đó thuộc distributed/runtime service layer. Đặc biệt: IPC ≠ networking IPC ≠ distributed computing IPC ≠ message broker IPC có thể sử dụng socket transport nhưng socket chỉ là implementation detail. | 0832 §604.2 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8125 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Các primitive chính: Core IPC cung cấp: Endpoint Channel Message Request Response Stream Event SharedRegion SharedBuffer Handle Peer Service Subscription Các primitive này phải có ABI ổn định. | 0832 §604.3 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8126 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Endpoint: Endpoint xác định một điểm giao tiếp. Khái niệm: Endpoint scheme name namespace security transport Ví dụ: ipc://app/service ipc://user/cache ipc://system/logger Không expose trực tiếp OS-specific naming vào application API. | 0832 §604.4 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8127 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Endpoint namespace: Có ba namespace: ProcessLocal User System Ví dụ: ipc://process/foo ipc://user/myapp/cache ipc://system/service Application không được tự ý tạo endpoint thuộc namespace cao hơn capability được cấp. | 0832 §604.5 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8128 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Endpoint identity: Endpoint identity gồm: EndpointId ServiceName InstanceId Namespace Generation `Generation` giúp tránh nhầm endpoint cũ sau khi service restart. | 0832 §604.6 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8129 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Service: Service là logical owner của một hoặc nhiều endpoint. Ví dụ: service ImageProcessor { fn resize(image: Image, width: u32, height: u32) -> Image } Compiler có thể sinh: ImageProcessorClient ImageProcessorServer ImageProcessorMessage ImageProcessorCodec | 0832 §604.7 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8130 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Struct-only service model: Axiom không cần class để xây service. Ví dụ: struct ImageProcessor { workers: u32 } fn process(self: ImageProcessor, image: Image) -> Result<Image> IPC binding chỉ coi function có metadata service là RPC method. @ipc fn process(self: ImageProcessor, image: Image) -> Result<Image> `self` không phải object reference đặc biệt. Nó vẫn là tham số struct bình thường. | 0832 §604.8 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8131 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Method identity: Mỗi IPC method có: ServiceId MethodId SchemaVersion Không sử dụng tên string làm identifier runtime chính. | REQ-ECO-8132 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Channel: Channel là đường truyền hai chiều logic: Peer A ←→ Channel ←→ Peer B Channel có: send() recv() close() cancel() Channel không nhất thiết tương ứng 1:1 với OS socket/pipe. | 0832 §604.10 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8133 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — One-way channel: Cho event/fire-and-forget: channel.send(event) Không tạo response queue nếu không cần. Điều này giảm: - memory; - context switching; - bookkeeping. | 0832 §604.11 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8134 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Request/response: RPC semantics: request → response Mỗi request có: RequestId MethodId Payload Deadline Flags Response: RequestId Status Payload Flags | 0832 §604.12 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8135 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Request ID: `RequestId` là 128-bit logical identifier hoặc dạng compact 64-bit trong fast path. Runtime phải chống collision trong phạm vi channel. | 0832 §604.13 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8136 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Streaming: Một request có thể trả nhiều chunk: request ↓ chunk ↓ chunk ↓ chunk ↓ complete Không cần gom toàn bộ stream vào RAM. API: stream.next() stream.cancel() | 0832 §604.14 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |

| REQ-ECO-8139 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Message size: Không có message size vô hạn. Mỗi endpoint có: max_message_size max_queue_bytes max_inflight_requests Giá trị mặc định phải bounded. Application có thể tăng thông qua capability/configuration phù hợp. | 0832 §604.17 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8140 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Serialization: Axiom IPC serialization sử dụng binary encoding mặc định. Không dùng: - JSON; - XML; - reflection runtime nặng; cho fast-path native IPC. Text encoding chỉ là adapter. | 0832 §604.18 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |

| REQ-ECO-8144 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Endianness: Wire format sử dụng một endian canonical. Native endian chỉ được dùng trong shared-memory structures khi region có ABI descriptor tương ứng. | 0832 §604.22 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8145 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Schema identity: Mỗi schema có: SchemaId Version Fingerprint Fingerprint được compiler tạo deterministic. Ví dụ: SchemaId = hash(canonical_schema_definition) | 0832 §604.23 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8146 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Schema evolution: Cho phép: - thêm field; - bỏ field; - field optional; - enum extension; - version negotiation. Không cho phép silently thay đổi meaning của field cũ. | 0832 §604.24 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
| REQ-ECO-8147 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unknown fields: Decoder phải có khả năng: ignore unknown field khi schema cho phép. Điều này giúp rolling upgrade. | 0832 §604.25 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |

| REQ-ECO-8426 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Design conclusion: BOOTSTRAP-604 biến IPC thành một **typed, capability-aware, schema-versioned, zero-copy-capable native subsystem** thay vì chỉ là wrapper quanh socket/pipe. Đường đi tối ưu của Axiom là: typed API ↓ compile-time schema ↓ generated codec ↓ inline/small-message fast path ↓ native transport và đối với dữ liệu lớn: typed buffer ↓ SharedRegion ↓ capability transfer ↓ zero-copy access Điểm quan trọng là toàn bộ mô hình vẫn giữ nguyên triết lý của Axiom: explicit ownership explicit capability explicit lifetime bounded resources compile-time metadata native performance no mandatory GC no raw cross-process pointers | 0832 §604.304 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |

Runtime phải **không biến thành một operating system thu nhỏ**. OS vẫn chịu trách nhiệm về process primitive. | REQ-ECO-8731 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Architectural conclusion: BOOTSTRAP-605 hoàn thiện lớp **process/service lifecycle** phía trên IPC. Axiom giờ có một chuỗi native infrastructure tương đối đầy đủ: 600  State / Persistence / Recovery 601  Configuration / Secrets / Deployment 602  Logging / Diagnostics / Crash 603  Security / Capability / Permissions 604  IPC / Shared Memory / Transport 605  Process / Service Supervision / Watchdog Điểm quan trọng là các lớp này không trở thành một runtime monolith. Chúng vẫn có thể được compile/link theo module: Application ├── Core only ├── Core + Config ├── Core + Diagnostics ├── Core + IPC ├── Core + Supervisor └── Full Native Runtime Axiom vì vậy vẫn giữ được mục tiêu: native fast small explicit bounded capability-safe no mandatory GC no mandatory broker no hidden ownership | 0833 §605.303 | - | EPIC(E24.9) |
